title: Spelling rules for adding endings

match.reason: The bank point teaches general strategies for unfamiliar words (syllables and word parts) and mentions only one ending rule as an example, while the new point is specifically about the rules for doubling consonants, dropping silent e and changing y to i when adding endings.

draft.title: Spelling rules for adding endings
card: Doubling
If a short word ends in one vowel then one consonant, double the consonant before an ending that starts with a vowel. Run becomes running and hop becomes hopping.
Dropping e
If a word ends in a silent e, drop the e before an ending that starts with a vowel. Make becomes making and hope becomes hoping.
Y to i
If a word ends in a consonant then y, change the y to i before most endings. Happy becomes happiness and carry becomes carried.
Check the end of the base word first, then pick the pattern that fits. If none fits, just add the ending, as in jump and jumping.
draft.remember: Look at how the base word ends, then double, drop or change before you add the ending.

a.q: Which spelling of the word made from stop plus -ing is correct?
opts: stopping
stoping
stopeing
stoppping
a.why: Stop ends in one vowel then one consonant, so the p is doubled before -ing. Stoping is tempting, but it leaves out the doubling and would suggest a long o sound.
a.clue: Count the vowels and consonants at the end of stop.

b.q: Mia adds -ness to the word busy to describe how a café feels. Which spelling is correct, and why?
opts: Business, because the y changes to i
Busyness, because the y stays the same
Busiiness, because the i is doubled
Busness, because the y is dropped
b.why: Busy ends in a consonant then y, so the y changes to i before the ending. Busyness is tempting because the ending is added with no change, but this pattern needs the y to change.
b.clue: Look at the letter before the y in busy.

b.best: Busyness, because the y stays the same

problems.detail: The intended answer, business, is wrong here. Business means commerce or a company. The word for how busy a café feels is busyness, a recognised exception that keeps the y. The question marks the correct spelling wrong and teaches a false spelling.

Why (b) says busyness is wrong because the pattern needs the y to change. It calls the real word for the state of being busy an error. The card only says the y changes before most endings, so the why also overstates the rule.

The remember line says to double, drop or change before adding the ending. This suggests one of the three always applies, but the card says to just add the ending when none fits, as in jump and jumping.
